name: Leaf Miner (Vegetable Leaf Miner)
description: Small fly larvae that create winding tunnels within leaf tissue of leafy vegetables and other crops. The mines reduce photosynthetic capacity, spoil the marketability of leafy greens, and can cause severe defoliation.
symptoms: Serpentine winding white or translucent tunnels in leaves
Dark frass trail visible within mines
Leaf tissue around mines turning yellow and necrotic
Premature leaf drop in heavy infestations
Reduced market quality of leafy vegetables
treatments: Remove and destroy mined leaves (effective for small infestations)
Apply spinosad or abamectin when mining is first observed
Use neem oil or insecticidal soap as preventive spray
Introduce parasitic wasps (Diglyphus isaea, Dacnusa sibirica)
Install yellow sticky traps for adult monitoring
prevention: Use floating row covers to exclude adult flies
Practice crop rotation with non-host crops
Remove and destroy crop debris promptly after harvest
Avoid broad-spectrum insecticides that kill natural enemies
Monitor regularly with yellow sticky traps
